user.title: Swiss Solar Forecast
user.description: Where is the plant? Your Home Assistant location is pre-filled: move the marker onto the roof, or type a street address (the federal address register knows every address of Switzerland). The next step lists the roof planes of that building from the Sonnendach cadastre of the Federal Office of Energy; you tick every plane that carries modules, then enter the figures of each plane one after the other. One entry is one plant: one inverter with its strings. A second inverter at the same place is a second entry with another name.

data_description.yield_sensor: An energy sensor that counts what the modules of this entry produce, all of them and no others (total or daily counter, Wh, kWh or MWh). Not a meter that also counts a second plant, and not the same meter in two entries. With it the forecast corrects itself: it learns what the model cannot know (shading by trees or buildings, soiling), today's figure takes the hours the meter has already counted, and you see how accurate the forecast was. Can be set or changed later under Configure.

roofs.title: Roof planes
roofs.description: {count} roof plane(s) at {place} in the Sonnendach cadastre, largest first: orientation, tilt, area, suitability class (1 low … 5 top) and the long-term electricity yield of the whole plane. Tick every plane that carries modules. The last entry, "Add a new plane by hand", is for a roof the cadastre does not know, a garage on another building or a ground-mounted plant: you then enter orientation and tilt yourself. Tick it together with the others if you need both; further planes by hand are added later with Reconfigure, one at a time.

plane.title: Plane {index} of {total}
plane.description: Roof: {roof}. Orientation and tilt come from the cadastre; correct them if you know better. Enter the installed peak power of this plane in kWp (the cadastre's area would hold about {kwp_hint} kWp with modern modules). Losses cover wiring, inverter, soiling and mismatch (14 % is a usual figure). Damping scales the result, for calibration against your real yield.

reconfigure.title: Move the plant or change its planes
reconfigure.description: Move the marker or type another address; the roof planes there are listed next, together with the planes the plant already has (all of them ticked, the ones entered by hand included), then the figures of every plane with the current values pre-filled. The entry keeps its entities, their ids and history.

reconfigure_roofs.title: Roof planes
reconfigure_roofs.description: {count} roof plane(s) at {place} in the Sonnendach cadastre, largest first. Below them are the plant's planes the cadastre does not list here, the ones entered by hand among them, with name, peak power and orientation. Everything the plant has now is ticked: leave a tick to keep the plane, remove it to remove the plane. The last entry adds one new plane by hand; for more than one, run Reconfigure again.

reconfigure_plane.title: Plane {index} of {total}
reconfigure_plane.description: Plane: {roof}. The figures are the plane's current ones where the plant already has it, else the cadastre's suggestion.

error.cannot_connect: The federal geo service could not be reached. Check the internet connection and try again.
error.no_match: No address matches the text. Try street and place, or move the marker instead.
error.pick_one: Tick at least one plane, or the last entry to enter one by hand.
error.meter_in_use: This meter already calibrates the entry "{entry}". A meter has to count the modules of exactly one entry: pick the meter that counts this plant alone, or leave the field empty.

abort.already_configured: A plant with this name is already set up at this place. Use its Reconfigure to change the planes, or give a second inverter another name.
abort.cannot_connect: The MeteoSwiss open data could not be read. Check the internet connection and try again.

init.title: What do you want to change?
init.description: A plane for its figures (peak power, orientation, tilt, losses, damping), or the whole plant for the inverter limit, the yield meter and the corrections. To add or remove planes, or move the plant, use Reconfigure in the entry's menu.

plane.title: Plane {plane}
plane.description: Peak power, orientation, tilt, losses and damping of this plane. Changing a value reloads the entry; entity ids and history are kept. Use damping to calibrate: if the forecast is 10 % too high over a few sunny weeks, set 0.9.

plant.title: The whole plant
plant.description: The AC limit of the inverter: the hourly forecast of all strings together is clipped at it. Set it to the inverter's rated AC power.

data.station_correction: Correction from a measurement station nearby

data_description.terrain_horizon: Reads the horizon of the place once from the swisstopo elevation model. While the sun stands behind a mountain or a valley side, only the diffuse light counts. Bare terrain only: trees and buildings are not in the model.
data_description.snow: Follows the snow from the forecast: precipitation that falls as snow covers the modules, and they produce nothing until it has slid off or melted. Steep modules clear sooner than flat ones. An estimate; with a yield meter, modules that produce although the forecast shows them covered are set free at once.
data_description.station_correction: While the sun is up, the radiation the nearest MeteoSwiss measurement station recorded in the last hour is compared with the forecast for the same time. The difference corrects the current hour and, fading out, the next three. Only with a station within 25 km at a similar height; costs one small request every 15 minutes during the day.
data_description.yield_sensor: An energy sensor that counts what the modules of this entry produce, all of them and no others (total or daily counter, Wh, kWh or MWh). Not a meter that also counts a second plant, and not the same meter in two entries. Every hour the forecast is compared with what was counted, and a factor per place of the sun in the sky is learned: shading by trees or buildings, soiling, whatever the model does not know. It follows the sun and not the clock, so what was learned holds when the days grow longer or shorter. Hours that are over count in today's figure with what the meter counted. Hours with snow on the modules are left out. With the meter you also see how accurate the forecast was over the last 7 and 30 days. Leave empty to switch the self-calibration off; another meter or changed figures of a plane start the learning anew.

error.meter_in_use: This meter already calibrates the entry "{entry}". A meter has to count the modules of exactly one entry: pick the meter that counts this plant alone, or leave the field empty.

abort.no_planes: This plant has no planes; set it up again.

options.manual: Add a new plane by hand

forecast_unreachable.title: Swiss Solar Forecast: forecast not readable
forecast_unreachable.description: The MeteoSwiss open data could not be read for several refreshes in a row ({error}). Check your internet connection; if it is fine, the MeteoSwiss service is down or has changed. The sensors stay unavailable until then and recover on their own; this notice disappears with the next successful refresh.
